name: WLOS News 13

access.robots: User-agent * allows /. GPTBot, ClaudeBot, anthropic-ai, Claude-Web, Google-Extended, CCBot, ChatGPT-User, Applebot-Extended, cohere-ai are Disallow: /. No sitemap in robots; /sitemap.xml is section pages only.

qualityWhy: The highest-volume Asheville newsroom (#1 Asheville publisher in the Google News gap check). The raw Local feed is ~93% western NC and ~46% Asheville/Buncombe; after the module's Buncombe filter, ~90% of what it keeps is Buncombe. Original reporting, including News 13 Investigates and Ask 13.
recommendationWhy: Best single mainstream source for volume and freshness, and the feed can be filtered to Buncombe reliably because WLOS URL slugs are stuffed with place names.
testResult: OK wlos - 19 articles (Buncombe filter kept 19 of 41), published 2026-09-23..2026-09-25; summary 100% | contentText 0% | image 100% | author 0% | categories 0%; fetchFullText ok 3/3 (811, 6,368, 3,857 chars); a separate pass over the other 16 was 16/16 ok, no HTML
notes: The feed holds ~41 items (~2.2 days). Each has title, a one-sentence dek and a 16x9 enclosure image, but no body, byline or useful category (all 'article'). The Buncombe filter (mentionsBuncombe in lib/news/sources/shared/buncombe.ts) tests title + dek + URL slug against a place regex (Asheville except 'Asheville Highway', Buncombe, Black Mountain, Swannanoa, Weaverville, Woodfin, Montreat, Biltmore, Candler, Leicester, Fairview, Arden, Enka, Barnardsville, Skyland, Oteen, Montford, River Arts District, UNCA, A-B Tech, Mission Hospital, Warren Wilson). Known leaks: slug stuffing lets through a few non-Buncombe stories (e.g. Pisgah Inn with '...-asheville-business'). Known drops: WNC-wide stories that never name a Buncombe place (Gov. Stein's WNC recovery plan; Bounty & Soul in Black Mountain, whose slug only says 'wnc'). fetchFullText reads the page's StoryText_storyText block rather than JSON-LD articleBody, which loses paragraphs, keeps “ entities and inlines the all-caps related-story headlines. It strips ad slots (AdUnit), image/video embeds with captions (Embed_), and all-caps link-only 'related story' paragraphs. The dateline ('ASHEVILLE, N.C. (WLOS) -') is kept. Sinclair's terms (sbgi.net/terms-conditions) forbid using 'mining, scraping, data extraction or other tools'; the owner decided on 2026-09-25 to store full text internally with summary-only display.

name: Blue Ridge Public Radio

access.robots: Disallows /post/, /term/, /topic/, /programs/, /npr-news/ only. Section feeds and article paths are allowed. No AI-crawler blocks. Sitemaps: /sitemap.xml, /sitemap-latest.xml, /news-sitemap-content.xml (mostly NPR national).

qualityWhy: Asheville's NPR station, with the deepest local public-affairs reporting in this category: Asheville City Council and Buncombe commissioners write-ups, Helene recovery, health systems, environment. Bylines, deks and lead images are all present.
recommendationWhy: An Asheville-based newsroom: ~55% of stories are Asheville/Buncombe, and the rest is regional politics that bears on Asheville (Rep. Chuck Edwards, FEMA/WNC funding, state election law). So it is not geo-filtered. Free, and nothing in robots or terms stands in the way.
testResult: OK bpr - 9 articles, published 2026-09-14..2026-09-23; summary 100% | contentText 44% (from the Local News feed) | image 100% | author 100% | categories 100%; fetchFullText ok 3/3 (6,715, 3,371, 3,345 chars)
notes: Grove/Brightspot CMS (NPR's platform). /index.rss is empty. Every section has /<slug>.rss with its newest 10 items; stories appear in several sections, so scrape() merges 8 feeds by URL and records every section as a category (8 feed GETs at 1/sec, ~9s). Only bpr-news.rss ('Local News') carries content:encoded. fetchFullText reads .ArtP-articleBody from the article page, with figures/captions and .Enh related-story cards stripped. The window is 14 days because BPR files only ~5-8 local stories a week. REJECTED sub-feed: /local-nc-news.rss ('Regional & State News') is the NC Public Radio Association pool (WFAE, WUNC, WFDD bylines, tagged NCPRA), mostly statewide. BPR's copyright page is DMCA-only; I found no ToS clause about automated access.

name: FOX Carolina (WHNS)

access.robots: User-agent * allows /news/ and doesn't disallow /arc/outboundfeeds/rss. GPTBot, ClaudeBot, anthropic-ai, Claude-Web, Google-Extended, CCBot, PerplexityBot, Bytespider etc. are Disallow: /.

qualityWhy: A Greenville SC station with a real western NC bureau. Mostly short Buncombe crime, courts and public-safety stories, with full body and bylines in the feed; it often has cases WLOS lacks and corroborates the rest.
recommendationWhy: Arc's NC section feed plus a Buncombe filter (title + dek + lede/dateline) gives ~1.3 Buncombe stories/day with full text in a single request. The raw section is only ~32% Buncombe, so the filter is essential.
testResult: OK foxcarolina - 10 articles (Buncombe filter), published 2026-09-18..2026-09-25; summary 100% | contentText 100% (avg 1,479 chars) | image 100% | author 100% | categories 0%
notes: Arc XP outboundfeeds; `size=30` covers ~9 days. The site-wide feed is Upstate SC plus national (~5% WNC). /category/news/north-carolina/ is the WNC desk, but Gray sister stations (WBTV, WECT, Atlanta News First, Axios Charlotte) also file there; items whose dateline credits another outlet are dropped even if they mention Asheville. Filtered with mentionsBuncombe (lib/news/sources/shared/buncombe.ts), the same helper wlos.ts uses. The module strips Instagram/Twitter/TikTok embeds and the 'MORE NEWS:' / 'Feel more informed... download our apps' promo paragraphs. Known leak: station self-promo that names the 'Asheville market'. Gray's Terms of Use s.8(j) bar using AI/scrapers to 'access, collect, copy, index, store' content; the owner decided on 2026-09-25 to store full text internally with summary-only display.

name: Black Mountain News

access.robots: The same Gannett robots.txt as citizen-times.com: anthropic-ai, Claude*, ClaudeBot, GPTBot, CCBot, Google-Extended and ~40 others are Disallow: /. User-agent * allows /story/. Sitemaps: /news-sitemap.xml, /web-sitemap-index.xml.

qualityWhy: The only paper dedicated to the Swannanoa Valley (Black Mountain, Swannanoa, Montreat, all in Buncombe): town council, local elections, Helene rebuilding, the 'Valley Rewind' history column. Staffed by a Citizen-Times reporter.
recommendationWhy: 100% Buncombe, and unlike citizen-times.com it serves plain fetches. Stories are metered but marked isAccessibleForFree, which the owner ruled readable on 2026-09-25, so the full body is stored.
testResult: OK blackmountainnews - 3 articles, published 2026-09-21..2026-09-24; summary 100% | contentText 100% (avg 2,522 chars) | image 100% | author 67% | categories 100% | paywalled 0%
notes: Gannett has no RSS. scrape() reads the monthly web sitemap on gannett-cdn.com (1-2 GETs; only the paper's own stories, ~13-18 a month, none of the USA TODAY network filler the homepage mixes in) and keeps URLs with lastmod inside 7 days. It then GETs each story page (~3-4 per run at 1/sec) for its JSON-LD NewsArticle: headline, description (dek), datePublished, author, image, keywords ('tag:Swannanoa', ...). That same page gives the body: .gnt_ar_b minus asides (ads, related cards), figures and the ul.gnt_sh highlights box, which keeps paragraphs, h2 subheads and lists. The JSON-LD has no articleBody. Since scrape() already has the page, there is no separate fetchFullText. Stories are 'access:metered' but JSON-LD says isAccessibleForFree=true; the owner ruled on 2026-09-25 that metered-but-free is readable. paywalled is set only when isAccessibleForFree === false, and then no body is kept. Gannett's 'tag:Overall Positive/Negative' sentiment labels are dropped. sourceId is Gannett's numeric asset id. On 2026-09-25 blackmountainnews.com returned 200 to plain Node and to curl with either the Chrome/120 or Chrome/140 UA, while citizen-times.com and blueridgenow.com returned 402 to the same requests, so the wall is per-property rather than per-client.

name: Asheville Citizen-Times

feedUrls: https://www.gannett-cdn.com/sitemaps/PASH/web/web-sitemap-YYYY-MM.xml (not fetched; URL pattern inferred from Black Mountain News)
access.robots: Explicitly Disallow: / for anthropic-ai, Claude, Claude-Web, claudeweb, ClaudeBot, Claude-User, Claude-SearchBot, GPTBot, ChatGPT-User, OAI-SearchBot, PerplexityBot, Google-Extended, CCBot, Applebot, Diffbot, Scrapy and ~40 more. User-agent * disallows /feeds/, /services/, /search, /content-queries/ etc.

qualityWhy: The paper of record and the largest newsroom (Gannett); #2 Asheville publisher in the Google News gap check. It would be the top source on journalism alone.
recommendationWhy: Every non-browser client is refused with HTTP 402, and robots.txt names Claude and every major AI agent. Getting in would mean evading a deliberate block.
notes: The homepage, news-sitemap.xml and the legacy rssfeeds host all return 402 'Access Restricted' to plain Node (Chrome/120 and the new Chrome/140 NEWS_USER_AGENT), to the Chrome-TLS undici dispatcher with either UA, and to curl. WebFetch was refused. robots.txt itself returns 200, so this is a bot wall, not an outage. Black Mountain News is the same Gannett platform and is NOT walled, so it is built separately. Gannett's CDN sitemaps (the PASH equivalent of Black Mountain's PBMN) probably list Citizen-Times URLs, but the story pages themselves are behind the 402, so all we'd have is URL slugs. I didn't pursue it: it would be working around the block. For headlines + links, the Google News source (community scout) is the sanctioned path.

qualityWhy: A Spartanburg SC Nexstar station. The main feed is ~20/day, mostly Upstate SC plus Nexstar national wire. Its Asheville-tagged posts (~1/day) are mostly brief crime and courts rewrites of APD/BCSO/DA releases that WLOS and FOX Carolina also run.

WP REST posts?tags=551,4233,2718 returned 50 posts back to 2026-08-04 with full content.rendered and featured images; the embedded author is empty. Some posts carry 80KB+ of embed markup. name: Charlotte Observer + News & Observer (McClatchy)

access.robots: ClaudeBot, anthropic-ai, Claude-Web, Claude-SearchBot, GPTBot, Google-Extended are Disallow: /*.html (i.e. all stories). Sitemaps include /sitemap/story/googlenews.xml and /sitemap/topic/archive.xml.

qualityWhy: Strong statewide papers that cover Asheville on big stories (Helene housing money, state funding fights), usually with a Raleigh angle local outlets don't have. The two papers share one story pool (same article ids).
recommendationWhy: No Asheville section or topic feed. Filtering the site-wide feed (~31/day each) to Buncombe keeps ~1 story every 2 days, the same story in both papers, headline + dek only because of the paywall. Cheap to build if the owner wants the statewide angle.
notes: The stories feeds are RSS with title, dek, image, author and keyword categories (e.g. 'Asheville housing recovery'), but no body. The Buncombe regex over title + dek + categories matched 1 of 53 (Observer) and 1 of 54 (N&O), the same article317335711, during Helene-anniversary week. The Google News gap check counted 24 combined items in 7 days, which likely includes passing body mentions that a feed-level filter can't see. /sitemap/topic/archive.xml has no Asheville/WNC topic. If built: one module over both feeds, deduped by the numeric article id, paywalled: true.
